headline: Medium-risk pair: Botpress can ingest content while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and calls APIs, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can call APIs. If PaddleOCR output or extracted text is fed into Botpress, file content can be treated as trusted instructions. The pairwise bridge is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into Botpress prompts or knowledge sources
IF Botpress ingests document text without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction hierarchy to all imported OCR text
Disable automatic ingestion of OCR output into Botpress prompts
Review one sample document flow for prompt-like strings before rollout
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from OCR to Botpress inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted network egress, while Botpress has no documented network egress but is a support agent that may handle user content. A shared workspace or manual transfer could expose document contents to the OCR pipeline and then into Botpress outputs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same documents or images
IF OCR outputs are forwarded into Botpress transcripts or logs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate folders
Turn off retention of OCR intermediates where possible
Redact sensitive fields before OCR runs
Check outbound API destinations for PaddleOCR integrations
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and PaddleOCR can run browsers with allowlisted egress, but neither profile shows shared write access, git state, or overlapping mutable resources. A conflict is possible only if an operator wires them to the same workspace or automation target. Because the write surface is not documented, severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or repo
IF browser automation from PaddleOCR mutates artifacts Botpress also edits
mitigations: Keep package installs and browser automation in separate sandboxes
Avoid shared git working trees
Use a single orchestrator lock for any shared artifact
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted document text, and Botpress is a support agent likely to consume that text in downstream conversations. If Botpress treats OCR output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not document verification controls, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress uses OCR output as source material without verification
IF extracted text is surfaced to end users or automation
mitigations: Require human review for low-confidence OCR fields
Show source snippets alongside extracted answers
Add a verification step before Botpress replies
Limit automation to non-destructive actions
requires-engineering: propagate confidence scores end-to-end

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress and PaddleOCR both appear open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. PaddleOCR touches documents and images, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes or cross-border handling. Because compliance gaps are not evidenced, this is a low-risk documentation gap rather than a breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through either agent
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Document data classes handled by each agent
Confirm retention settings for OCR intermediates
Review deployment region and vendor terms
Add a compliance checklist before enabling regulated data
